Research information

Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey
Department of Neurosurgery, New Brunswick, NJ

Mechanisms of Human Memory in Online General Populations

You are invited to take part in a research study at Rutgers University. Participation is completely voluntary.

Purpose. To understand how people remember past experiences.

What you will do. You will complete one online memory task (videos, a memory test, and short music ratings) on Pavlovia. The session takes about 60 minutes.

Payment. You will receive $12.00 per hour through Prolific when you finish.

Risks. Risks are minimal: mild eye strain, boredom, or tiredness from a computer task. There are rest breaks between blocks.

Benefits. There is no direct benefit to you. The study may help researchers understand memory.

Privacy. We do not collect your name, IP address, medical information, or contact details. Research records use only the temporary Prolific ID from the study link.

Leaving the study. You may skip any survey question or stop at any time by closing this window.

Questions. For questions about your rights as a participant, contact the Rutgers Human Research Protection Program, 335 George Street, Liberty Plaza Suite 3200, New Brunswick, NJ 08901. Phone: (848) 932-0150. Email: irb-office@research.rutgers.edu.

By clicking I AGREE, you confirm that:

  1. You have read and understood this information.
  2. You are at least 18 years old and fluent in English.
  3. You voluntarily agree to participate.
  4. You may print or save a copy of this form.

Print or save a copy

TEST MODE — short experimenter run (3 trials).

Welcome to the memory task

This study takes about 60 minutes in one sitting. Please use a desktop or laptop with a keyboard and working audio (headphones or speakers). Phones and tablets will not work.

The session has three parts:

  1. Part 1 — Videos. You will watch short video clips. Some play with music in the background. Between clips, look at the fixation cross (+). While each video plays, press F if there is one person or fewer or J if there is more than one person (count people only). Try to remember the videos.
  2. Part 2 — Memory test. You will see videos and decide whether each is OLD (seen in Part 1) or NEW (not seen before). LEFT arrow = OLD    RIGHT arrow = NEW. Then rate how sure you are. If you say OLD, you will also answer a short question about music.
  3. Part 3 — Music ratings. You will hear again each piece of music that played with a video. Each clip lasts about 6 seconds. Then you will answer four short questions by clicking a number from 1 to 5. Each question moves on after 4 seconds.

Before Part 1 and again before Part 3, there is a short audio check. You will also see brief breaks between blocks. Press ENTER to advance instruction screens.
